grades.quote: Implementations are permitted to resume execution for any reason, even if an enabled interrupt has not become pending. Hence, a legal implementation is to simply implement the WFI instruction as a NOP.
grades.reason: The passage is about RISC-V WFI, not condition variables. It does give a loosely analogous rule: WFI may resume without an actionable event (it can even be a NOP), so software must re-check the condition and loop back. That is the same reasoning behind a while loop around a condition-variable wait (spurious wakeups). It never mentions condition variables or while loops, so it only helps by analogy.
